# PostHog analytics in a separate Website and API

Use this when adding browser and backend analytics to the repository pattern.
This is an optional capability, not part of every generated scaffold. Start from
the questions, collection policy and accepted loss budget, then follow the
[Alchemy resource guide](../providers/posthog.md) and
[Effect browser adapter](../../../effect-client-wrapper/references/posthog-browser.md).
Keep product analytics separate from request logs, traces and operational metrics.
Apply the sibling [strict Effect policy](../../../strict-effect-ts/SKILL.md) to
schemas, services, adapters, infrastructure and tests; the SDK does not grant a
whole analytics folder an exception.

## Contents

- [Put each responsibility with its owner](#put-each-responsibility-with-its-owner)
- [Make the Effect contract reviewable](#make-the-effect-contract-reviewable)
- [Count backend work separately](#count-backend-work-separately)
- [Keep a browser relay on the owning Website](#keep-a-browser-relay-on-the-owning-website)
- [Verify the assembled capability](#verify-the-assembled-capability)

## Put each responsibility with its owner

Adapt these paths to the target repository; they are an ownership map rather
than a requirement to create every file:

```text
packages/analytics/src/
  schemas.ts                 checked settings, event vocabulary and brands
  errors.ts                  closed capture failures
  service.ts                 named browser/backend operations
  live.layer.ts              native backend HTTP capture
  test.layer.ts              deterministic service implementation
packages/infrastructure/src/posthog/
  schemas.ts / errors.ts / service.ts
  management.adapter.layer.ts  private Distilled operations and credentials
  resources.ts / dashboards.ts  resource lifecycle and desired chart catalogue
  bindings.egress.ts            checked stage-specific deployment outputs
apps/web/src/lib/analytics/
  browser.adapter.layer.ts   private SDK lifecycle
  capture.consumer.ts        synchronous checked before-send callback
  relay/
    schemas.ts / errors.ts / service.ts
    live.layer.ts            one native outbound HTTP attempt
    body.ingress.ts          bounded byte reader
    request.ingress.ts       checked Website HTTP request
    response.egress.ts       native response adaptation
apps/api/src/
  analytics.layer.ts         request-scoped collection and finalisation
alchemy.posthog.run.ts       composition-only resource stack
```

Packages import explicit package exports and never app internals. The existing
server runtime composes the relay service; the React-owned Atom runtime composes
the browser service. The native API entry composes backend capture with its
incoming request Effect fibre. No analytics package starts a runtime or shares
mutable per-request state across users.

## Make the Effect contract reviewable

- Public operations return `Effect.Effect<Success, AnalyticsError, never>` with
  Schema-derived inputs and outputs. Capture transport, configuration and SDK
  dependencies in the Layer; typecheck the real implementation against
  `Service.of`. Native request handlers may retain documented host requirements;
  those requirements must not leak into the shared analytics service.
- Use named `Effect.fn("Service.operation")` with a generator directly for
  sequential public work. Use `Effect.fnUntraced` for reusable private work that
  belongs to the caller's span. Keep pure total transformations plain. Split
  files by schema/error/service/transport ownership, not one helper per SDK call.
- Decode stage, host, token and collection mode with their owning Schema.
  Model enabled/disabled settings as a closed union: disabled needs no fake key
  or placeholder host. Invalid enabled settings are a named configuration
  failure, not configured-off. If startup must remain available, make the
  downgrade a reported policy at composition, separate from deliberate disable.
- Decode external absence to `Option` once and prefer `Option.match` for both
  branches. Do not access `.value`, inspect `_tag` or use unsafe extraction.
  Use `Boolean.match` for boolean choices and `Match.exhaustive` for closed
  states; do not introduce Option solely to hide a boolean decision. Return
  nullable values only at a host contract that explicitly requires them.
- Decode incoming data and encode owned outgoing payloads in their ingress and
  egress owners. No assertions, raw JSON, raw fetch, ambient environment reads,
  clocks, timers, random globals or raw Promise orchestration. The browser's
  named SDK adapter and synchronous consumer are the documented host exceptions;
  backend HttpClient and Distilled calls remain native Effect.
- Map expected SDK/HTTP/codec failures to closed Schema-tagged errors with safe
  operation/reason fields. Best-effort capture catches those named errors at
  its application owner. Do not erase configuration, permission or decode
  failure with blanket `Effect.option`/`Effect.ignore`, convert it with `orDie`,
  or catch all Causes to report success. Preserve interruption and defects.
  Discarding an invalid optional campaign field is a separate, explicit policy.
- Create `Ref`s and any concurrency limits during the intended Layer/request
  lifetime. Use scoped acquisition and bounded finalisers. No mutable module
  client, request accumulator, per-click runner or detached fibre. Logging and
  span fields use safe fixed names; event bodies and visitor IDs stay out.

## Count backend work separately

Collect a bounded set of domain outcomes in a request-local `Ref`, then send one
request-completed event and those outcomes together. Define whether health,
preflight, discovery and streamed responses count. Pick a truthful completion
point for streams and cancellation; do not count a stream twice or claim the
body was delivered merely because response headers exist.

Use native Effect `HttpClient` for capture rather than adding a server SDK solely
to send batches. Check and encode the owned wire Schema; distinguish accepted
HTTP responses, rejection and transport failure. Bound the entire send and keep
resources scoped. Use Effect Clock/Random for timing and event identity; do not
introduce ambient clocks or random globals. Worker CPU timing can differ from
provider-measured latency, so name the recorded duration accurately.

On native Alchemy Cloudflare Workers, use the installed
`WorkerExecutionContext.waitUntil(effect)` API for bounded background sends.
It extends request work and preserves the native Effect context without a new
runner in owned code. Call it while the native request context is valid. The
installed Alchemy implementation captures the calling services; it does not
extend every service's acquisition scope. Close over only dependencies that
remain alive for the send and open the HTTP send scope inside the background
Effect. Do not carry a soon-to-close request scope or raw host context into a
second runtime. Test request finalisation while the controlled send is pending.
It is not a persistent queue or a promise of delivery after termination.
Expected analytics failure should not change the application's response when
best-effort loss is the agreed policy. Keep fixed safe diagnostics and separate
backend request IDs from browser visitor IDs. Do not add retries without deciding
how duplicates are prevented and how long sends may live.

## Keep a browser relay on the owning Website

For a minimal browser client, an existing Website path such as `/ingest/e/` avoids
another Worker and cross-origin delivery to `api.<domain>`. A thin TanStack route
calls a native Effect HTTP program through the existing server runner. This is
fixed provider ingress for the Website's browser client, not a domain API or a
second Content/HTTP/RPC implementation. It is the narrow exception to keeping
backend machine routes out of the Website. A separate proxy Worker or API route
is valid when isolation or other requirements justify it; decide that explicitly.

Set the browser SDK's checked `api_host` to the Website path. Backend capture
can stay direct to its fixed regional ingestion host. The relay reduces direct
analytics-domain blocking even for explicit events; it cannot recover events
that never reach it or defeat every blocker. Preserve chosen privacy controls.

Qualify the pinned SDK's actual endpoint, media types, compression, query keys,
batch delay, retry policy and response handling. The source-derived SDK used
`/e/`, roughly three-second batches, gzip bytes labelled `text/plain`, plus JSON
and form fallbacks. Those are version-specific observations, not universal
PostHog endpoints. Enabling flags, replay or external scripts introduces paths
that this minimal relay deliberately does not support; revisit the protocol
before enabling them. Do not proxy arbitrary URLs or guessed assets.

Keep the relay small but check its real boundary:

- Fixed POST path, fixed regional upstream and allowed Website origin. Origin
  checking is a browser policy, not authentication for a public project token.
- Checked retry/compression query, rejecting duplicates and unknown keys.
  Use Schema optional-to-Option codecs and `Option.match`; encode query keys
  only at the outgoing boundary.
- Unchanged bytes, UUIDs and timestamps. Do not parse and rebuild SDK batches
  merely to forward them. The owning Schema checks protocol metadata and bounded
  bytes; the browser consumer separately owns allowed event properties.
- Native `Stream.limitBytes` bounds both request and reply even without
  Content-Length. Supply a typed failing fallback when the limit is crossed:
  `Stream.empty` would silently accept a truncated body. Test the exact limit
  and the crossing chunk; never forward a partially collected oversized batch.
  No manual mutable byte counter. Compressed-byte limits do not establish
  decompressed event size; the forwarding relay does not decompress.
- One scoped deadline covers request body, upstream headers and reply body.
  The source pattern chose 1 MiB per body and five seconds; choose limits for the
  target application's actual payloads and runtime constraints.
- Rebuild allowed headers. Strip caller cookies, auth, IP forwarding and trace
  headers; disable native HttpClient trace propagation. Configure the native
  transport for manual redirects before sending, then reject every 3xx response
  without forwarding its Location. Rejecting a final status is insufficient if
  the transport has already followed it. In the qualified FetchHttpClient,
  `RequestInit` is read at execution and its Layer uses `layerMergedContext` to
  carry acquisition settings into requests. Providing manual redirects to that
  Layer is supported; verify the actual call retains that setting and no caller
  overrides it. Do not add `followRedirects`.
- Preserve upstream success/error statuses and checked retry headers; return
  `no-store`. Do not report a failed provider attempt as successful delivery.

Keep SDK retries as the single retry owner for this design. Forward each attempt
once with no relay retry, durable queue or direct-send fallback unless explicitly
designed. Browser batching still leaves a loss window on tab closure. Give relay
requests their own telemetry category so they do not inflate API/domain counts.

## Verify the assembled capability

Typecheck live and test implementations at the same closed service contract.
Check the error channel and Layer input/output types; a signature made clean by
an assertion or `orDie` is not proof. Use `@effect/vitest` for Effect tests and
Effect FileSystem/ChildProcess for test work; no raw async setup or real sleeps.

Use the actual lint command and negative fixtures to reject SDK access outside
the browser adapter, Promise bridges outside named host adapters, misplaced
codecs, manual tag checks and unchecked optional extraction. Split large files
by their schemas/service/error/transport owners; do not create forwarding helpers.

Test unchanged bytes and supported formats, status handling, stripped headers,
exact/oversized bodies without Content-Length, a stalled incoming body, late
headers followed by a stalled reply, interruption and resource cleanup. Native
HttpClient may represent a bodyless response as a typed empty-body error; qualify
and handle that case without masking other stream failures. Prove one upstream
attempt and closed service requirements with deterministic Layers/TestClock.
Test redirect refusal with a real local native transport as well as a fake
HttpClient: a fake returning 302 cannot prove the real client never followed it.
Cover late completion after timeout, concurrent requests with separate state,
request-scope closure during background sending and safe drop diagnostics.

Reject an implementation until enabled/disabled configuration, each named error,
Schema round-trips, lifecycle, concurrency and the actual lint prohibitions have
been checked. Missing live delivery evidence must remain a stated non-claim.

Then follow the resource guide's delivery sequence: controlled enabled Preview,
fresh browser requests, exact stored UUIDs and backend events, temporary domain
blocking and client retries when relevant, restored privacy overrides and disabled
ordinary Preview, and separately authorised production plan/apply/readback.
Local tests, HTTP 200, provider state and stored-event queries are separate proof.
Keep a dated receipt in the application repository; do not copy its account IDs,
personal details, tokens or deployment-specific findings into reusable skills.

See [PostHog proxy guidance](https://posthog.com/docs/advanced/proxy) and
[native Alchemy Worker source](https://github.com/alchemy-run/alchemy/tree/main/packages/alchemy/src/Cloudflare/Workers).

# PostHog analytics in a separate Website and API

Use this when adding browser and backend analytics to the repository pattern.
This is an optional capability, not part of every generated scaffold. Start from
the questions, collection policy and accepted loss budget, then follow the
[Alchemy resource guide](../providers/posthog.md) and
[Effect browser adapter](../../../effect-client-wrapper/references/posthog-browser.md).
Keep product analytics separate from request logs, traces and operational metrics.
Apply the sibling [strict Effect policy](../../../strict-effect-ts/SKILL.md) to
schemas, services, adapters, infrastructure and tests; the SDK does not grant a
whole analytics folder an exception.

## Contents

- [Put each responsibility with its owner](#put-each-responsibility-with-its-owner)
- [Make the Effect contract reviewable](#make-the-effect-contract-reviewable)
- [Count backend work separately](#count-backend-work-separately)
- [Keep a browser relay on the owning Website](#keep-a-browser-relay-on-the-owning-website)
- [Verify the assembled capability](#verify-the-assembled-capability)

## Put each responsibility with its owner

Adapt these paths to the target repository; they are an ownership map rather
than a requirement to create every file:

```text
packages/analytics/src/
  schemas.ts                 checked settings, event vocabulary and brands
  errors.ts                  closed capture failures
  service.ts                 named browser/backend operations
  live.layer.ts              native backend HTTP capture
  test.layer.ts              deterministic service implementation
packages/infrastructure/src/posthog/
  schemas.ts / errors.ts / service.ts
  management.adapter.layer.ts  private Distilled operations and credentials
  resources.ts / dashboards.ts  resource lifecycle and desired chart catalogue
  bindings.egress.ts            checked stage-specific deployment outputs
apps/web/src/lib/analytics/
  browser.adapter.layer.ts   private SDK lifecycle
  capture.consumer.ts        synchronous checked before-send callback
  relay/
    schemas.ts / errors.ts / service.ts
    live.layer.ts            one native outbound HTTP attempt
    body.ingress.ts          bounded byte reader
    request.ingress.ts       checked Website HTTP request
    response.egress.ts       native response adaptation
apps/api/src/
  analytics.layer.ts         request-scoped collection and finalisation
alchemy.posthog.run.ts       composition-only resource stack
```

Packages import explicit package exports and never app internals. The existing
server runtime composes the relay service; the React-owned Atom runtime composes
the browser service. The native API entry composes backend capture with its
incoming request Effect fibre. No analytics package starts a runtime or shares
mutable per-request state across users.

## Make the Effect contract reviewable

- Public operations return `Effect.Effect<Success, AnalyticsError, never>` with
  Schema-derived inputs and outputs. Capture transport, configuration and SDK
  dependencies in the Layer; typecheck the real implementation against
  `Service.of`. Native request handlers may retain documented host requirements;
  those requirements must not leak into the shared analytics service.
- Use named `Effect.fn("Service.operation")` with a generator directly for
  sequential public work. Use `Effect.fnUntraced` for reusable private work that
  belongs to the caller's span. Keep pure total transformations plain. Split
  files by schema/error/service/transport ownership, not one helper per SDK call.
- Decode stage, host, token and collection mode with their owning Schema.
  Model enabled/disabled settings as a closed union: disabled needs no fake key
  or placeholder host. Invalid enabled settings are a named configuration
  failure, not configured-off. If startup must remain available, make the
  downgrade a reported policy at composition, separate from deliberate disable.
- Decode external absence to `Option` once and prefer `Option.match` for both
  branches. Do not access `.value`, inspect `_tag` or use unsafe extraction.
  Use `Boolean.match` for boolean choices and `Match.exhaustive` for closed
  states; do not introduce Option solely to hide a boolean decision. Return
  nullable values only at a host contract that explicitly requires them.
- Decode incoming data and encode owned outgoing payloads in their ingress and
  egress owners. No assertions, raw JSON, raw fetch, ambient environment reads,
  clocks, timers, random globals or raw Promise orchestration. The browser's
  named SDK adapter and synchronous consumer are the documented host exceptions;
  backend HttpClient and Distilled calls remain native Effect.
- Map expected SDK/HTTP/codec failures to closed Schema-tagged errors with safe
  operation/reason fields. Best-effort capture catches those named errors at
  its application owner. Do not erase configuration, permission or decode
  failure with blanket `Effect.option`/`Effect.ignore`, convert it with `orDie`,
  or catch all Causes to report success. Preserve interruption and defects.
  Discarding an invalid optional campaign field is a separate, explicit policy.
- Create `Ref`s and any concurrency limits during the intended Layer/request
  lifetime. Use scoped acquisition and bounded finalisers. No mutable module
  client, request accumulator, per-click runner or detached fibre. Logging and
  span fields use safe fixed names; event bodies and visitor IDs stay out.

## Count backend work separately

Collect a bounded set of domain outcomes in a request-local `Ref`, then send one
request-completed event and those outcomes together. Define whether health,
preflight, discovery and streamed responses count. Pick a truthful completion
point for streams and cancellation; do not count a stream twice or claim the
body was delivered merely because response headers exist.

Use native Effect `HttpClient` for capture rather than adding a server SDK solely
to send batches. Check and encode the owned wire Schema; distinguish accepted
HTTP responses, rejection and transport failure. Bound the entire send and keep
resources scoped. Use Effect Clock/Random for timing and event identity; do not
introduce ambient clocks or random globals. Worker CPU timing can differ from
provider-measured latency, so name the recorded duration accurately.

On native Alchemy Cloudflare Workers, use the installed
`WorkerExecutionContext.waitUntil(effect)` API for bounded background sends.
It extends request work and preserves the native Effect context without a new
runner in owned code. Call it while the native request context is valid. The
installed Alchemy implementation captures the calling services; it does not
extend every service's acquisition scope. Close over only dependencies that
remain alive for the send and open the HTTP send scope inside the background
Effect. Do not carry a soon-to-close request scope or raw host context into a
second runtime. Test request finalisation while the controlled send is pending.
It is not a persistent queue or a promise of delivery after termination.
Expected analytics failure should not change the application's response when
best-effort loss is the agreed policy. Keep fixed safe diagnostics and separate
backend request IDs from browser visitor IDs. Do not add retries without deciding
how duplicates are prevented and how long sends may live.

## Keep a browser relay on the owning Website

For a minimal browser client, an existing Website path such as `/ingest/e/` avoids
another Worker and cross-origin delivery to `api.<domain>`. A thin TanStack route
calls a native Effect HTTP program through the existing server runner. This is
fixed provider ingress for the Website's browser client, not a domain API or a
second Content/HTTP/RPC implementation. It is the narrow exception to keeping
backend machine routes out of the Website. A separate proxy Worker or API route
is valid when isolation or other requirements justify it; decide that explicitly.

Set the browser SDK's checked `api_host` to the Website path. Backend capture
can stay direct to its fixed regional ingestion host. The relay reduces direct
analytics-domain blocking even for explicit events; it cannot recover events
that never reach it or defeat every blocker. Preserve chosen privacy controls.

Qualify the pinned SDK's actual endpoint, media types, compression, query keys,
batch delay, retry policy and response handling. The source-derived SDK used
`/e/`, roughly three-second batches, gzip bytes labelled `text/plain`, plus JSON
and form fallbacks. Those are version-specific observations, not universal
PostHog endpoints. Enabling flags, replay or external scripts introduces paths
that this minimal relay deliberately does not support; revisit the protocol
before enabling them. Do not proxy arbitrary URLs or guessed assets.

Keep the relay small but check its real boundary:

- Fixed POST path, fixed regional upstream and allowed Website origin. Origin
  checking is a browser policy, not authentication for a public project token.
- Checked retry/compression query, rejecting duplicates and unknown keys.
  Use Schema optional-to-Option codecs and `Option.match`; encode query keys
  only at the outgoing boundary.
- Unchanged bytes, UUIDs and timestamps. Do not parse and rebuild SDK batches
  merely to forward them. The owning Schema checks protocol metadata and bounded
  bytes; the browser consumer separately owns allowed event properties.
- Native `Stream.limitBytes` bounds both request and reply even without
  Content-Length. Supply a typed failing fallback when the limit is crossed:
  `Stream.empty` would silently accept a truncated body. Test the exact limit
  and the crossing chunk; never forward a partially collected oversized batch.
  No manual mutable byte counter. Compressed-byte limits do not establish
  decompressed event size; the forwarding relay does not decompress.
- One scoped deadline covers request body, upstream headers and reply body.
  The source pattern chose 1 MiB per body and five seconds; choose limits for the
  target application's actual payloads and runtime constraints.
- Rebuild allowed headers. Strip caller cookies, auth, IP forwarding and trace
  headers; disable native HttpClient trace propagation. Configure the native
  transport for manual redirects before sending, then reject every 3xx response
  without forwarding its Location. Rejecting a final status is insufficient if
  the transport has already followed it. In the qualified FetchHttpClient,
  `RequestInit` is read at execution and its Layer uses `layerMergedContext` to
  carry acquisition settings into requests. Providing manual redirects to that
  Layer is supported; verify the actual call retains that setting and no caller
  overrides it. Do not add `followRedirects`.
- Preserve upstream success/error statuses and checked retry headers; return
  `no-store`. Do not report a failed provider attempt as successful delivery.

Keep SDK retries as the single retry owner for this design. Forward each attempt
once with no relay retry, durable queue or direct-send fallback unless explicitly
designed. Browser batching still leaves a loss window on tab closure. Give relay
requests their own telemetry category so they do not inflate API/domain counts.

## Verify the assembled capability

Typecheck live and test implementations at the same closed service contract.
Check the error channel and Layer input/output types; a signature made clean by
an assertion or `orDie` is not proof. Use `@effect/vitest` for Effect tests and
Effect FileSystem/ChildProcess for test work; no raw async setup or real sleeps.

Use the actual lint command and negative fixtures to reject SDK access outside
the browser adapter, Promise bridges outside named host adapters, misplaced
codecs, manual tag checks and unchecked optional extraction. Split large files
by their schemas/service/error/transport owners; do not create forwarding helpers.

Test unchanged bytes and supported formats, status handling, stripped headers,
exact/oversized bodies without Content-Length, a stalled incoming body, late
headers followed by a stalled reply, interruption and resource cleanup. Native
HttpClient may represent a bodyless response as a typed empty-body error; qualify
and handle that case without masking other stream failures. Prove one upstream
attempt and closed service requirements with deterministic Layers/TestClock.
Test redirect refusal with a real local native transport as well as a fake
HttpClient: a fake returning 302 cannot prove the real client never followed it.
Cover late completion after timeout, concurrent requests with separate state,
request-scope closure during background sending and safe drop diagnostics.

Reject an implementation until enabled/disabled configuration, each named error,
Schema round-trips, lifecycle, concurrency and the actual lint prohibitions have
been checked. Missing live delivery evidence must remain a stated non-claim.

Then follow the resource guide's delivery sequence: controlled enabled Preview,
fresh browser requests, exact stored UUIDs and backend events, temporary domain
blocking and client retries when relevant, restored privacy overrides and disabled
ordinary Preview, and separately authorised production plan/apply/readback.
Local tests, HTTP 200, provider state and stored-event queries are separate proof.
Keep a dated receipt in the application repository; do not copy its account IDs,
personal details, tokens or deployment-specific findings into reusable skills.

See [PostHog proxy guidance](https://posthog.com/docs/advanced/proxy) and
[native Alchemy Worker source](https://github.com/alchemy-run/alchemy/tree/main/packages/alchemy/src/Cloudflare/Workers).

# Common Practice

Use plain, simple Australian English. Explain code in concrete words.

Read [README.md](README.md), [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md), and
[the documentation index](docs/README.md) before changing the repository.

## Mandatory implementation rules

Apply [.agents/skills/strict-effect-ts/SKILL.md](.agents/skills/strict-effect-ts/SKILL.md)
to **all owned code**, including tests, scripts, configuration and infrastructure.
Use Effect for every operation that can fail or perform work outside the program.
Use Effect Schema to check inputs and outputs and branded types for identifiers,
paths and meaningful strings at boundaries. Keep errors typed and named.

No raw async/await or Promise workflows, try/catch, throws, fetch, process.env,
unchecked JSON, unchecked array indexing, assertions, unsafe Option extraction,
ambient clocks, or mutable global collections. Prefer Effect primitives first.
Plain JSX and deterministic framework declarations are allowed.
The only command runtimes are `tools/references/sync.runtime.ts` and
`tools/checks/docs.runtime.ts`; test execution belongs to @effect/vitest.
The frontend runtime is `apps/web/src/lib/runtime.server.ts`: one runtime whose
single runner every TanStack entry point uses. Keep TanStack response adaptation
there. The Website calls its same-stage API through
`apps/web/src/lib/api/binding.adapter.layer.ts`, the narrow Cloudflare Promise adapter.
The native API entry `apps/api/src/deployment/cloudflare/worker.ts` composes
Content, the private renderer and shared transport Layers. Its HTTP handler runs
in the incoming request's Effect fibre without another Promise runner. Do not
pass Effect Context through TanStack or add another frontend runtime.
Image SDK calls stay in `apps/api/src/og/takumi.adapter.layer.ts`.
PostHog browser SDK calls stay in `apps/web/src/lib/analytics/browser.adapter.layer.ts`;
Distilled management calls stay in `packages/infrastructure/src/posthog/management.adapter.layer.ts`.
Backend analytics uses Effect HttpClient and native Alchemy `waitUntil`.

Authored Markdown belongs to `@content/pages`. `@common-practice/content` owns its schemas,
errors, service, source loader and live/test Layers. HTTP, RPC and MCP reuse those
exports. No package imports an app. Keep one `getPage({ id, format })` operation,
with optional `format` defaulting to complete `data`; check the returned variant.
Frontend loaders preserve typed errors in a checked success/error envelope.

The browser runtime is `apps/web/src/lib/runtime.client.ts`, an Effect Atom
runtime mounted by React. Its Promise bridges are confined to
`apps/web/src/lib/webmcp/model-context.adapter.layer.ts` and the private browser
analytics adapter. PostHog's synchronous before-send callback is confined to
`apps/web/src/lib/analytics/capture.consumer.ts`; it uses a non-throwing Schema
check and returns only allowed fields. Browser content calls
use the public API and checked addresses from the root loader, not bundled
sources. WebMCP registers only at the matching Website origin. Remote MCP has a
separate public checked Origin/CORS policy. Keep server and browser runtime
imports inside TanStack's matching environment functions (`lib/browser-atom.ts`
is the browser one). Follow the ownership sections in ARCHITECTURE.md.

Apply [.agents/skills/alchemy-iac/SKILL.md](.agents/skills/alchemy-iac/SKILL.md)
to deployment work. Only the native Alchemy CLI may plan, deploy or destroy.
Never substitute Wrangler or provider API writes for Alchemy resource ownership.
Check `.references/alchemy` examples and installed types before implementation.
Check `.references/effect` for current Effect APIs. Run `bun run references:sync`
to verify both reference clones against the committed lock and package catalog.
Do not modify the reference clones or copy legacy Site patches blindly.

Every dependency must have an exact current, compatible release recorded in the
root catalogs or manifest. Refresh registry metadata before changing versions.
Follow [version decisions](docs/standards/dependencies.md); latest Effect v4 RC is
intentional because native Alchemy v2 uses Effect v4.

## Checks and boundaries

Run `bun run verification` before claiming the local implementation passes.
The build generates TanStack's route tree; never edit that generated file.
Keep `tools/oxlint/vendor` byte-for-byte reference copies, with provenance and
rule dispositions in [lint policy](docs/standards/lint.md). New rules and tests
must follow Effect. Never disable a failing safety rule just to get green checks.
Prove important prohibitions using the actual Oxlint command and negative fixtures.

Keep local checks, browser checks, Cloudflare deployment and public URL checks
as separate evidence. A local build does not prove a working deployment.
Credentials belong in Doppler; never print them, commit them, or forward the
whole environment into a Worker. The Website declares its bindings explicitly:
`COMMON_PRACTICE_STAGE`, its stage-specific `BACKEND` service binding, `COMMON_PRACTICE_API_URL`,
`COMMON_PRACTICE_WEBSITE_URL`, `COMMON_PRACTICE_POSTHOG_CONFIG`, plus Common Practice's scoped
Axiom telemetry values on hosted stages only. Both Workers use native Alchemy
ownership and deploy together; Preview APIs must never point to production.
Do not adopt existing cloud resources or configure a public domain by guesswork.

Before changing an area, read its owning document. Update that document when
behaviour changes; do not create competing instructions. Preserve unrelated work.

# A PostHog browser client owned by Effect

Use this for a PostHog client in a React/TanStack application with an Effect
Atom runtime. It complements the
[app and proxy layout](../../alchemy-iac/references/effect/posthog-analytics.md)
and [Alchemy provider guide](../../alchemy-iac/references/providers/posthog.md).
Inspect the installed SDK and Effect APIs; this describes a qualified pattern,
not a version-independent implementation to paste. Apply the sibling
[strict Effect policy](../../strict-effect-ts/SKILL.md), including its named
operations, closed requirements, typed errors and narrow host exceptions.

## Contents

- [Keep the public service semantic](#keep-the-public-service-semantic)

wrong origin, Do Not Track, allowed events/properties, acknowledgement failure,

[collection controls](https://posthog.com/docs/privacy/data-collection) and the

# TaxKit repository guide

TaxKit is the public monorepo for the open-source tax engine, API, SDK, and
documentation site. Start with [`docs/README.md`](docs/README.md), the sole
maintainer-document lifecycle and truth-layer router. `CLAUDE.md` points to this
file; edit `AGENTS.md` only.

## Operating loop

1. Read `docs/README.md`, then only the semantic owner for the task.
2. Confirm the claim against code, configuration, Schemas, exports, generated
   owners, or external readback at the boundary it describes.
3. Put current implementation intent in a SPEC/task and active execution plan;
   never reopen completed work as policy.
4. Update the earliest durable owner and required pointers in the same slice.
5. Run `bun run check:docs`, `bun run check:runbooks` when operations changed,
   focused checks, and `bun run verification`;
   package-facing changes also need an appropriate Changeset.
6. Retain artifact identity, authority, postconditions, limitations,
   non-claims, and rollback.

For any material calculator/rule/schema, SDK/export/example, HTTP/OpenAPI,
public MDX/navigation/runtime, package/app, command/CI/versioning/release-proof,
lifecycle, SPEC, plan, runbook, or skill change, invoke the repository-local
`$docs-maintainer` route before accepting the slice. Record `Change required`,
`Preserve`, or evidenced `N/A` for its documentation impact. Scheduled or
background freshness work is report-only candidate output unless a separately
attached implementation authority names the reviewer and publisher.

## Task routes

- Repository and package topology:
  [`docs/architecture/README.md`](docs/architecture/README.md), then
  [`docs/architecture/package-ownership.md`](docs/architecture/package-ownership.md).
- Effect services and boundaries:
  [`docs/architecture/effect-services.md`](docs/architecture/effect-services.md)
  and the applicable package README.
- API/SDK: [`docs/architecture/api-and-sdk.md`](docs/architecture/api-and-sdk.md),
  [`apps/api/README.md`](apps/api/README.md), and
  [`packages/sdk/typescript/README.md`](packages/sdk/typescript/README.md).
- Calculators/rules/facts: the focused owner under `docs/architecture/` and the
  owning package README.
- Frontend/public docs:

  and [`apps/docs/README.md`](apps/docs/README.md).

## Engineering guardrails

- Use Effect-native Schema, branded identities, Config, services, Layers,
  tagged errors, collections, Command, and runtime primitives when they own the
  semantics. Decode unknown/representation ingress once and encode egress at
  explicit boundaries.
- Reuse owning Schemas and schema-derived types. Do not mirror raw `id: string`,
  DTOs, provider types, primitive semantic config, or unchecked SDK output.
- Keep primary Effects flat, sequential, and pipe-first where that clarifies
  data flow. Keep one-use mapping/decoding/error logic inline; reject
  helper/common/utils sprawl and generic SDK callback wrappers.
- Keep service contracts, live Layers, test Layers, and executable composition
  separate. Do not run Effects or build live Layers inside domain logic.
- Provider clients expose named Effect operations, `Config.schema` with
  redacted secrets, immediate Schema decoding, safe tagged errors without
  `instanceof`, and live/mock Layers.
- React composition flows route → policy-owning container → focused leaf.
  Routes own transport restoration/outcome matching, containers own commands
  and coordination, and leaves render readonly values/local interaction state.
- Admit an abstraction only with semantic weight, an owner, a real reuse or
  substitution point, a simpler call graph, and focused proof.

## Authority and proof

Tool access is capability, not authority. Provider, registry, publication,
release, deployment, credential, and destructive operations require a named
principal, operation, resource, environment, approval boundary, receipt,
rollback/revocation, and readback. Local gates do not prove publication,
production, or external consumer behavior.

Use `bun run check:repository-paths` for checkout portability and
`bun run verification` for repository closeout. Use `bun run release:check`
only for its documented local release-evidence graph; it does not authorize or
prove publication.

Effect’s `latest` is stable `4.0.0`, while its `rc` tag is `rc.118` and `beta` is `beta.107`. Alchemy beta `.80` now declares `effect` and platform peers as `^4.0.0`. **The evidence points to an outdated accepted-version range, rather than a Scheduler API break.** This remains a proposed compatibility decision until the new app is tested.

Atom React `4.0.0` imports Scheduler in one source file and uses only:

- `unstable_scheduleCallback`
- `unstable_LowPriority`
- `unstable_cancelCallback`

It schedules a low-priority callback and returns a function that cancels that same task. All three exist in `0.28.0`. [Pinned Atom source](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/blob/effect%404.0.0/packages/atom/react/src/RegistryContext.ts)

More strongly, the published Scheduler **`0.27.0` and `0.28.0` default production and development implementations are byte-for-byte identical**. Production SHA-256 for both is `679adff761d31e9426604f80c0e99be44a3e6f4c6834b0218ecf0312a67c171f`; development and the production mock also match. Sources inspected directly: [Scheduler 0.27 tarball](https://registry.npmjs.org/scheduler/-/scheduler-0.27.0.tgz), [Scheduler 0.28 tarball](https://registry.npmjs.org/scheduler/-/scheduler-0.28.0.tgz).

Atom does not exchange task objects with React DOM or read React DOM’s Scheduler state. However, each Scheduler instance owns its own queue and priority state; React DOM reads that priority for message events. **Use one shared Scheduler `0.28.0` instance** to preserve coordination, rather than letting installation silently create separate `0.27` and `0.28` copies. [React DOM release metadata](https://registry.npmjs.org/react-dom/19.3.0)

Published Atom remains `4.0.0`; its accepted range and live upstream `main` still say `>=0.25.0 <0.28.0`. Targeted upstream searches found no relevant fix, although that does not prove none exists. [Atom release metadata](https://registry.npmjs.org/%40effect%2Fatom-react/4.0.0), [upstream manifest](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Effect-TS/effect/main/packages/atom/react/package.json)

I propose a **metadata-only patch** adding the exact tested release:

```text
>=0.25.0 <0.28.0 || 0.28.0
```

No runtime code patch is indicated.

The later clean fixture should prove:

1. Atom and React DOM resolve the same pinned Scheduler `0.28.0`, including the production browser bundle.
2. Scheduled Atom updates run, cancelled work stays cancelled, and rapid calculator changes show the newest result.
3. Server rendering and browser hydration work with the same versions.
4. React strict-mode mount/remount and final unmount correctly release Atom services and pending work. Account for the provider’s documented 500 ms delayed disposal.

No installation, patch, TaxKit edit or runtime qualification occurred in this research.

# TaxKit repository guide

TaxKit is the public monorepo for the open-source tax engine, API, SDK, and
documentation site. Start with [`docs/README.md`](docs/README.md), the sole
maintainer-document lifecycle and truth-layer router. `CLAUDE.md` points to this
file; edit `AGENTS.md` only.

## Operating loop

1. Read `docs/README.md`, then only the semantic owner for the task.
2. Confirm the claim against code, configuration, Schemas, exports, generated
   owners, or external readback at the boundary it describes.
3. Put current implementation intent in a SPEC/task and active execution plan;
   never reopen completed work as policy.
4. Update the earliest durable owner and required pointers in the same slice.
5. Run `bun run check:docs`, `bun run check:runbooks` when operations changed,
   focused checks, and `bun run verification`;
   package-facing changes also need an appropriate Changeset.
6. Retain artifact identity, authority, postconditions, limitations,
   non-claims, and rollback.

For any material calculator/rule/schema, SDK/export/example, HTTP/OpenAPI,
public MDX/navigation/runtime, package/app, command/CI/versioning/release-proof,
lifecycle, SPEC, plan, runbook, or skill change, invoke the repository-local
`$docs-maintainer` route before accepting the slice. Record `Change required`,
`Preserve`, or evidenced `N/A` for its documentation impact. Scheduled or
background freshness work is report-only candidate output unless a separately
attached implementation authority names the reviewer and publisher.

## Task routes

- Repository and package topology:
  [`docs/architecture/README.md`](docs/architecture/README.md), then
  [`docs/architecture/package-ownership.md`](docs/architecture/package-ownership.md).
- Effect services and boundaries:
  [`docs/architecture/effect-services.md`](docs/architecture/effect-services.md)
  and the applicable package README.
- API/SDK: [`docs/architecture/api-and-sdk.md`](docs/architecture/api-and-sdk.md),
  [`apps/api/README.md`](apps/api/README.md), and
  [`packages/sdk/typescript/README.md`](packages/sdk/typescript/README.md).
- Calculators/rules/facts: the focused owner under `docs/architecture/` and the
  owning package README.
- Frontend/public docs:
  [`docs/architecture/frontend.md`](docs/architecture/frontend.md),
  [`docs/architecture/content-and-posts.md`](docs/architecture/content-and-posts.md),
  and [`apps/docs/README.md`](apps/docs/README.md).
- Current work: [`docs/product-specs/index.md`](docs/product-specs/index.md) and
  [`docs/exec-plans/active/README.md`](docs/exec-plans/active/README.md).
- Standards, tests, and release checks:
  [`docs/standards/README.md`](docs/standards/README.md) and
  [`docs/architecture/testing-and-quality.md`](docs/architecture/testing-and-quality.md).
- Repeatable release, versioning, packed-consumer and recovery operations:
  [`docs/runbooks/README.md`](docs/runbooks/README.md) and
  [`docs/operations/authority-model.md`](docs/operations/authority-model.md).
- References and audits: [`docs/references/README.md`](docs/references/README.md)
  and [`docs/documentation-audit/README.md`](docs/documentation-audit/README.md).

## Engineering guardrails

- Use Effect-native Schema, branded identities, Config, services, Layers,
  tagged errors, collections, Command, and runtime primitives when they own the
  semantics. Decode unknown/representation ingress once and encode egress at
  explicit boundaries.
- Reuse owning Schemas and schema-derived types. Do not mirror raw `id: string`,
  DTOs, provider types, primitive semantic config, or unchecked SDK output.
- Keep primary Effects flat, sequential, and pipe-first where that clarifies
  data flow. Keep one-use mapping/decoding/error logic inline; reject
  helper/common/utils sprawl and generic SDK callback wrappers.
- Keep service contracts, live Layers, test Layers, and executable composition
  separate. Do not run Effects or build live Layers inside domain logic.
- Provider clients expose named Effect operations, `Config.schema` with
  redacted secrets, immediate Schema decoding, safe tagged errors without
  `instanceof`, and live/mock Layers.
- React composition flows route → policy-owning container → focused leaf.
  Routes own transport restoration/outcome matching, containers own commands
  and coordination, and leaves render readonly values/local interaction state.
- Admit an abstraction only with semantic weight, an owner, a real reuse or
  substitution point, a simpler call graph, and focused proof.

## Authority and proof

Tool access is capability, not authority. Provider, registry, publication,
release, deployment, credential, and destructive operations require a named
principal, operation, resource, environment, approval boundary, receipt,
rollback/revocation, and readback. Local gates do not prove publication,
production, or external consumer behavior.

Use `bun run check:repository-paths` for checkout portability and
`bun run verification` for repository closeout. Use `bun run release:check`
only for its documented local release-evidence graph; it does not authorize or
prove publication.

item.stdout:
# Architecture

The Website renders Home, About and a missing-page view. A separate API Worker
serves the same checked content to the Website and agents. The pages are still
placeholder content; there is no database or sign-in.

[ADR 0002](docs/adr/0002-api-owned-publishing.md) owns the accepted split and
[the implementation plan](docs/exec-plans/frontend-backend-split.md) records its
checks and delivery. [CONTEXT.md](CONTEXT.md) defines Page and Published page.

## Owners and imports

| Owner                                                         | Responsibility                                                                                                                 |
| ------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `content/pages` — `@content/pages`                            | Authored Markdown files, YAML metadata and source inventory                                                                    |
| `packages/content` — `@common-practice/content`               | Checked Page, PublishedPage, formats, errors, Content service, live/test Layers, parsing, publication metadata and image cache |
| `packages/http` — `@common-practice/http`                     | Native HTTP contract, handlers, clients, status mapping and shared response headers                                            |
| `packages/rpc` — `@common-practice/rpc`                       | Native RPC contract, handlers and client Layer                                                                                 |
| `packages/mcp` — `@common-practice/mcp`                       | Shared tool definitions/handlers, native remote MCP, resources, prompt and discovery card                                      |
| `packages/analytics` — `@common-practice/analytics`           | Checked capture settings, event vocabulary, closed browser/backend services and bounded native HTTP capture                    |
| `packages/infrastructure` — `@common-practice/infrastructure` | Shared deployment schemas, telemetry stacks, zone ownership, request observation and isolate identity                          |
| `apps/api` — `@common-practice/api`                           | Bundle authored sources, private Takumi renderer, API composition, publishing/discovery routes and native Worker               |
| `apps/web` — `@common-practice/web`                           | TanStack HTML, navigation, page heads, error states, private binding adapter and browser WebMCP host                           |

Each package has explicit source exports and no runtime of its own. Imports
between workspaces use those exports. No package imports an app. The root Bun
catalogs own exact shared versions. All owned code, including tests and
infrastructure, follows the strict Effect skill.

## A page request

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Web[Website route] --> Client[Content HTTP client]
  Agent[HTTP / RPC / MCP agent] --> Handler[Shared transport handler]
  Client --> Handler
  Handler --> Content[Content service and live Layer]
  Sources[Bundled authored Markdown] --> Content
  Content --> Image[Checked page sent to private renderer]
```

The API imports raw Markdown using Alchemy's native `?raw` loader. Content's
`live.layer.ts` parses and checks it once when the Layer is built. Invalid
metadata, unsupported Markdown or duplicate identities stop startup with a
named error. No source files are read during a request. The supported scaffold
body is one matching heading, one paragraph and its placeholder notice.

`Content.getPage({ id, format })` is one operation. Omitted `format` means
`data`, a complete PublishedPage with content, Markdown/image addresses and
search metadata. Explicit `markdown`, `og` and `seo` formats return those views.
Every response repeats `format`. Literal/default inputs have exact types;
a runtime choice returns a union that narrows when its `format` is checked.
One small schema-selected operation adapter is shared by both clients and
Content; it checks that the returned variant matches the request.

Schemas, derived types and named errors belong to Content. HTTP, RPC and MCP
reuse them. The native builders validate requests and encode outputs. Image
bytes use Effect's base64 codec on JSON transports and decode to checked PNG
bytes in typed clients. Expected errors decode to native tagged Effect errors.
A transport failure and an invalid response have separate named errors.

Both Content clients allow 40 seconds for each complete read, including the
reply body. Content owns this shared deadline. It leaves ten seconds beyond
the API's 30-second image limit for sending and checking the reply. Expiry
interrupts the pending call and returns the existing `ContentUnavailableError`
with its operation name; earlier caller cancellation stays interruption.
There is no automatic client retry.

Content reads a page once and passes the checked Page to its image service.
That service never calls Content. It owns a five-minute success cache, one
render permit and a 30-second timeout; failures expire immediately. The default
page response advertises the image address without rendering it. The API's
private Takumi adapter owns image SDK Promise calls. Browser PostHog calls stay
in the Website's private analytics adapter; backend capture uses native Effect
HttpClient rather than another SDK or Promise runner.

## Runtime and frontend loading

`apps/api/src/deployment/cloudflare/worker.ts` uses Alchemy's native Worker
class-and-`make` pattern. The lightweight class keeps the renderer and server
implementation out of Website bindings. Its native runtime builds Content,
images and routes once per isolate. `apps/api/src/application.layer.ts` checks
the API address and builds the native handler in Alchemy's instance Scope.
Shared services stay alive until that instance stops. Each request runs in its incoming Effect
fibre with its own cancellation, tracer and Scope. Streamed responses retain
that Scope until completion or cancellation. There is no API ManagedRuntime
or extra Promise runner.

Native Alchemy planning registers that Worker and its telemetry. It skips runtime
binding reads because Alchemy resolves `Worker.URL` only before upload. The native
`globalThis.__ALCHEMY_RUNTIME__` build flag removes deployment-only settings from
the uploaded bundle, so startup never asks for stack-only Stage or Zone services.
The native
`ALCHEMY_PHASE` selects startup of the real application after Alchemy supplies the
running Worker's checked bindings. Source validation and native bundle tests are
local proof; the public suite checks the uploaded application.

The Website keeps one server runtime at `apps/web/src/lib/runtime.server.ts`.
Every TanStack entry point uses its one runner and incoming cancellation signal.
`api/binding.adapter.layer.ts` immediately converts Cloudflare's required
service-binding Promise into Effect. It preserves the body stream and passes
Effect's abort signal; it does not clone the Request. The native HTTP client
provides the same Content service contract to page loaders. There is no local
backend fallback and no Effect Context passed through TanStack.

Page loaders return a checked success/error envelope. This preserves error tags
through TanStack's JSON serialisation, instead of throwing an error whose useful
fields would be lost. Routes render returned page text and metadata, or a named
error state. The Website has no authored page records or image renderer.

The browser has one Effect Atom runtime in `runtime.client.ts`, owned by React's
RegistryProvider. Checked Website/API addresses from the root server loader
initialise its Atom. The browser uses the public native HTTP client, with no
credentials and no redirects, and the same shared tool handlers. Unmounting
closes the tool registration Scope. `browser-atom.ts` reaches this runtime only
inside TanStack's client environment function; server rendering mounts an inert
Atom. No browser global is read during import.

The WebMCP host adapter registers only when the browser's exact origin matches
the deployed Website's checked self address. This includes its matching Preview
and local address. Remote MCP has a separate public Origin policy.

The only command runtimes are `tools/references/sync.runtime.ts` and
`tools/checks/docs.runtime.ts`. Tests run through `@effect/vitest`. Host Promise
exceptions are limited to the Website runner, its Cloudflare binding/span
adapter, the private Takumi adapter, the browser WebMCP host and the private
browser analytics adapter. PostHog's synchronous before-send callback is an
exact consumer: it returns a checked event containing only allowed fields, or
null. It never runs another Effect runtime.

## Public paths

| Website                                                        | API                                |
| -------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- |
| `/`, `/about` HTML                                             | `/pages`, `/pages/:id?format=data` |
| `/index.md`, `/about.md`                                       | `/pages/:id?format=markdown`       |
| `/.og`, `/about.og`                                            | `/pages/:id?format=og`             |
| HTML page heads                                                | `/pages/:id?format=seo`            |
| robots, sitemap, llms text, API catalogue, skills and MCP card | `/openapi.json`, `/rpc`, `/mcp`    |

Production's API base address is `https://api.withcommonpractice.com`.
The old API address remains a serving alias for existing clients.
The Website keeps canonical HTML, Markdown and image URLs. Discovery files and
cards advertise their own stage's API. Website representation routes choose
Content's requested format. Discovery routes forward through the same private
binding to API-owned publishing code. Legacy Website `/api/*`, `/rpc` and `/mcp`
routes are removed without aliases or redirects.

HTTP and RPC are public read-only APIs with credential-free CORS. The API allows
native Effect's `b3` and `traceparent` request headers, so the browser Content
client can read pages without disabling tracing. Remote MCP is anonymous and
broadly accessible to compatible agents, including valid
third-party browser origins. Its native transport supports the published
`2026-07-28` protocol. It accepts absent Origin or a valid serialised HTTP(S)
origin and rejects malformed or opaque origins before CORS, including preflight
requests. A small pinned Effect patch lets the existing native Origin check use
a checked predicate; no transport validation is bypassed. Compatibility and
connect/list/call behaviour require their own public checks.

## Joint deployment

`alchemy.run.ts` composes native Cloudflare/GitHub providers and Cloudflare-backed
state for the `daw` stack. Checked stages are `dev`, `preview`, `integration`,
`production` and `pr-<number>`. It deploys both apps together and returns checked
Website/API addresses as native stack outputs after Schema checks. The API
address feeds the Website binding through native `Output.mapEffect`, so Alchemy
can recognise an unchanged address while planning. An Action output would stay
unresolved and make that binding appear changed on every plan.

The Website stays a standard native `Cloudflare.Website.Vite`. Production retains
`common-practice-production`. The Common Practice cutover declaration makes
`withcommonpractice.com` canonical, with its `www`, the old
`departmentofagenticwork.com` apex and old `www` permanently redirecting to it.

keep separate retained resources; the old `DawZone` is never renamed or repurposed.
Preview stages reference production's Website via `preview.of`; they cannot
change its traffic and never set script `name` or `version.parent`.

The API retains logical resource `Backend` and physical name

declares `api.withcommonpractice.com` as primary and keeps
`api.departmentofagenticwork.com` serving the same Worker as an alias. API requests
are not redirected, so existing RPC and MCP POST clients keep working. Native
Alchemy resolves each exact hostname's own zone; a shared zone override is unsafe
across the two zones. Other hosted stages expose their own workers.dev address. Destroying
a Preview removes only its Website Preview and matching API.

Public content, canonical metadata and AI discovery use Common Practice and the
new website origin. Agent discovery lists `common-practice-website`; the former
`daw-website/SKILL.md` URL serves the same document for saved clients. Public MCP
identifies as `common-practice`, while its tool and prompt names stay stable.
Telemetry event names, runtime bindings, package names and stack identifiers stay
stable. The production trace filter includes both website origins to preserve
old traffic in the existing dashboards. These are source declarations; the
cutover checklist and dated evidence record deployment separately.

Native development runs Website port 3210 and API port 3211, both strict.
It needs the existing Doppler development credentials for Alchemy's state.
There is no single-app `dev:ui` fallback. The Website's native build hash includes
shared packages, content sources, API sources and the lockfile, so content-only
changes rebuild its version and refresh its cache.

The compatibility date is `2026-09-22`, with `nodejs_compat` and
`enable_request_signal`. Website bindings are explicitly `COMMON_PRACTICE_STAGE`, `BACKEND`,
`COMMON_PRACTICE_API_URL`, `COMMON_PRACTICE_WEBSITE_URL` and checked `COMMON_PRACTICE_POSTHOG_CONFIG`, plus scoped
Axiom values on hosted stages.
The API binds its checked stage and native self URL plus the same hosted
telemetry values. Preview never points at production's API. Deployment
credentials never become Worker bindings.

Shared zone, TLS, DNSSEC and crawler policy owners live in
`@common-practice/infrastructure`. The separate production-only `daw-observability` and
`daw-trace-export` stacks keep their existing names, shared Axiom outputs and
removal rules. This app split does not change their resources or dashboards.
Only native Alchemy may plan, apply or destroy. The
[deployment runbook](docs/runbooks/deployment.md) owns those procedures.

## Observability

`@common-practice/analytics` owns checked settings, capture events and the two
closed Effect services. The browser service is private to
`apps/web/src/lib/analytics/browser.adapter.layer.ts`, inside the existing Atom
runtime. It acquires the SDK automatically on enabled deployments, only at
the matching Website origin without Do Not Track. There is no consent UI,
stored choice or consent operation. The adapter removes the old Common Practice choice key
and clears any SDK opt-out left by the former controls without an opt-in event.
It disables automatic
capture, recordings, flags, surveys and person profiles. Its synchronous consumer

capture share an Effect semaphore, with consecutive duplicate page views skipped.
Scope closes the client on React unmount. Acquisition failure leaves the service
usable with capture off, preserving page loading and WebMCP.

The SDK sends its selected batches to the checked browser path `/ingest/e/`.
The Website's private `analytics/relay/live.layer.ts` forwards each attempt
once to fixed `https://us.i.posthog.com/e/` through native Effect HttpClient.
`runtime.server.ts` composes it in the existing runtime; the reserved TanStack
route uses that runtime's single runner. The boundary checks the deployment,
exact Website origin, path, method, query and media type. It preserves opaque
batch bytes, caps both bodies at 1 MiB and gives all body/delivery work five

`apps/api/src/deployment/cloudflare/worker.ts` uses Alchemy's native Worker
class-and-`make` pattern. The lightweight class keeps the renderer and server
implementation out of Website bindings. Its native runtime builds Content,
images and routes once per isolate. `apps/api/src/application.layer.ts` checks
the API address and builds the native handler in Alchemy's instance Scope.
Shared services stay alive until that instance stops. Each request runs in its incoming Effect
fibre with its own cancellation, tracer and Scope. Streamed responses retain
that Scope until completion or cancellation. There is no API ManagedRuntime
or extra Promise runner.

Native Alchemy planning registers that Worker and its telemetry. It skips runtime
binding reads because Alchemy resolves `Worker.URL` only before upload. The native
`globalThis.__ALCHEMY_RUNTIME__` build flag removes deployment-only settings from
the uploaded bundle, so startup never asks for stack-only Stage or Zone services.
The native
`ALCHEMY_PHASE` selects startup of the real application after Alchemy supplies the
running Worker's checked bindings. Source validation and native bundle tests are
local proof; the public suite checks the uploaded application.

The Website keeps one server runtime at `apps/web/src/lib/runtime.server.ts`.
Every TanStack entry point uses its one runner and incoming cancellation signal.
`api/binding.adapter.layer.ts` immediately converts Cloudflare's required
service-binding Promise into Effect. It preserves the body stream and passes
Effect's abort signal; it does not clone the Request. The native HTTP client
provides the same Content service contract to page loaders. There is no local
backend fallback and no Effect Context passed through TanStack.

Page loaders return a checked success/error envelope. This preserves error tags
through TanStack's JSON serialisation, instead of throwing an error whose useful
fields would be lost. Routes render returned page text and metadata, or a named
error state. The Website has no authored page records or image renderer.

The browser has one Effect Atom runtime in `runtime.client.ts`, owned by React's
RegistryProvider. Checked Website/API addresses from the root server loader
initialise its Atom. The browser uses the public native HTTP client, with no
credentials and no redirects, and the same shared tool handlers. Unmounting
closes the tool registration Scope. `browser-atom.ts` reaches this runtime only
inside TanStack's client environment function; server rendering mounts an inert
Atom. No browser global is read during import.

The WebMCP host adapter registers only when the browser's exact origin matches
the deployed Website's checked self address. This includes its matching Preview
and local address. Remote MCP has a separate public Origin policy.

The only command runtimes are `tools/references/sync.runtime.ts` and
`tools/checks/docs.runtime.ts`. Tests run through `@effect/vitest`. Host Promise
exceptions are limited to the Website runner, its Cloudflare binding/span
adapter, the private Takumi adapter, the browser WebMCP host and the private
browser analytics adapter. PostHog's synchronous before-send callback is an
exact consumer: it returns a checked event containing only allowed fields, or
null. It never runs another Effect runtime.

## Public paths

| Website                                                        | API                                |
| -------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- |
| `/`, `/about` HTML                                             | `/pages`, `/pages/:id?format=data` |
| `/index.md`, `/about.md`                                       | `/pages/:id?format=markdown`       |
| `/.og`, `/about.og`                                            | `/pages/:id?format=og`             |
| HTML page heads                                                | `/pages/:id?format=seo`            |
| robots, sitemap, llms text, API catalogue, skills and MCP card | `/openapi.json`, `/rpc`, `/mcp`    |

Production's API base address is `https://api.withcommonpractice.com`.
The old API address remains a serving alias for existing clients.
The Website keeps canonical HTML, Markdown and image URLs. Discovery files and
cards advertise their own stage's API. Website representation routes choose
Content's requested format. Discovery routes forward through the same private
binding to API-owned publishing code. Legacy Website `/api/*`, `/rpc` and `/mcp`
routes are removed without aliases or redirects.

HTTP and RPC are public read-only APIs with credential-free CORS. The API allows
native Effect's `b3` and `traceparent` request headers, so the browser Content
client can read pages without disabling tracing. Remote MCP is anonymous and
broadly accessible to compatible agents, including valid
third-party browser origins. Its native transport supports the published
`2026-07-28` protocol. It accepts absent Origin or a valid serialised HTTP(S)
origin and rejects malformed or opaque origins before CORS, including preflight
requests. A small pinned Effect patch lets the existing native Origin check use
a checked predicate; no transport validation is bypassed. Compatibility and
connect/list/call behaviour require their own public checks.

## Joint deployment

`alchemy.run.ts` composes native Cloudflare/GitHub providers and Cloudflare-backed
state for the `daw` stack. Checked stages are `dev`, `preview`, `integration`,
`production` and `pr-<number>`. It deploys both apps together and returns checked
Website/API addresses as native stack outputs after Schema checks. The API
address feeds the Website binding through native `Output.mapEffect`, so Alchemy
can recognise an unchanged address while planning. An Action output would stay
unresolved and make that binding appear changed on every plan.

The Website stays a standard native `Cloudflare.Website.Vite`. Production retains
`common-practice-production`. The Common Practice cutover declaration makes
`withcommonpractice.com` canonical, with its `www`, the old
`departmentofagenticwork.com` apex and old `www` permanently redirecting to it.
Native Alchemy preserves path and query on those redirects. Both verified zones
keep separate retained resources; the old `DawZone` is never renamed or repurposed.
Preview stages reference production's Website via `preview.of`; they cannot
change its traffic and never set script `name` or `version.parent`.

The API retains logical resource `Backend` and physical name
`common-practice-<stage>-backend`. Every stage owns an independent API Worker. Production
declares `api.withcommonpractice.com` as primary and keeps
`api.departmentofagenticwork.com` serving the same Worker as an alias. API requests
are not redirected, so existing RPC and MCP POST clients keep working. Native
Alchemy resolves each exact hostname's own zone; a shared zone override is unsafe
across the two zones. Other hosted stages expose their own workers.dev address. Destroying
a Preview removes only its Website Preview and matching API.

Public content, canonical metadata and AI discovery use Common Practice and the
new website origin. Agent discovery lists `common-practice-website`; the former
`daw-website/SKILL.md` URL serves the same document for saved clients. Public MCP
identifies as `common-practice`, while its tool and prompt names stay stable.
Telemetry event names, runtime bindings, package names and stack identifiers stay
stable. The production trace filter includes both website origins to preserve
old traffic in the existing dashboards. These are source declarations; the
cutover checklist and dated evidence record deployment separately.

Native development runs Website port 3210 and API port 3211, both strict.
It needs the existing Doppler development credentials for Alchemy's state.
There is no single-app `dev:ui` fallback. The Website's native build hash includes

The compatibility date is `2026-09-22`, with `nodejs_compat` and
`enable_request_signal`. Website bindings are explicitly `COMMON_PRACTICE_STAGE`, `BACKEND`,
`COMMON_PRACTICE_API_URL`, `COMMON_PRACTICE_WEBSITE_URL` and checked `COMMON_PRACTICE_POSTHOG_CONFIG`, plus scoped
Axiom values on hosted stages.
The API binds its checked stage and native self URL plus the same hosted
telemetry values. Preview never points at production's API. Deployment
credentials never become Worker bindings.

Shared zone, TLS, DNSSEC and crawler policy owners live in
`@common-practice/infrastructure`. The separate production-only `daw-observability` and
`daw-trace-export` stacks keep their existing names, shared Axiom outputs and
removal rules. This app split does not change their resources or dashboards.
Only native Alchemy may plan, apply or destroy. The
[deployment runbook](docs/runbooks/deployment.md) owns those procedures.

## Observability

`@common-practice/analytics` owns checked settings, capture events and the two
closed Effect services. The browser service is private to
`apps/web/src/lib/analytics/browser.adapter.layer.ts`, inside the existing Atom
runtime. It acquires the SDK automatically on enabled deployments, only at
the matching Website origin without Do Not Track. There is no consent UI,
stored choice or consent operation. The adapter removes the old Common Practice choice key

It disables automatic
capture, recordings, flags, surveys and person profiles. Its synchronous consumer

Scope closes the client on React unmount. Acquisition failure leaves the service
usable with capture off, preserving page loading and WebMCP.

The SDK sends its selected batches to the checked browser path `/ingest/e/`.
The Website's private `analytics/relay/live.layer.ts` forwards each attempt

`runtime.server.ts` composes it in the existing runtime; the reserved TanStack
route uses that runtime's single runner. The boundary checks the deployment,
